newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat Monday during holiday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat Monday during holiday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices were flat Monday, with activity diminished by a federal holiday and a lack of buyers as they waited for Tuesday's release of U.S. crude inventory figures, dealers said.
NYMEX February gasoline contracts settled 0.86 cents lower at 67.23 cents a gallon, under presure from milder weather forecasts which pushed down heating oil markets 1.50 cents to 66.94 cents.
"It's mostly a holiday for a lot of people," a trader said, referring to the Martin Luther King birthday holiday.
Traders saw the market turning weaker unless tomorrow's weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) shows lower inventories for the region.
January shipments of diesel fuels were nearly finished, brokers said, with gasolines expected to finish Wednesday.
Los Angeles CARB gasoline ranged 75/76 cents a gallon, unchanged from Friday, traders said, while February volumes were seen a penny higher.
Rack prices in L.A. were seen 74.25/75 cents a gallon, but buyers were wary of those prices going up.
Other conventional prices and distillates were stagnant Monday.
Brokers said they saw gasoline production falling off starting the second cycle of Februay, as RVP production ends.
